solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One getting around, hard and urgent — feature of US election campaign

indicators.note: turning around faces the other way, so the word for 'one' is written backwards

parts.note: one's self, the person; turned round it reads FLES
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a pressing matter is an urgent one

explanation.surface: Someone bustling about, tough and insistent, as candidates are on the American campaign trail.
explanation.walkthrough: SELF reversed gives FLES; add H and PRESSING to make FLESH-PRESSING.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the flesh means shaking hands with voters, a staple of American electioneering.

clue.text: What's strongly articulated with respect to rearing brood?

parts.note: 'for' can mean 'as regards'

indicators.note: rearing up in a down entry lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a hen broods or sits on eggs; written upwards it reads TIS

explanation.surface: A question about what a bird says forcefully concerning bringing up its chicks.
explanation.walkthrough: Fortis is a phonetics term for a consonant like p or t made with strong articulation; 'rearing' works upwards in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics a fortis consonant is pronounced with greater muscular tension and breath force than its lenis partner.

clue.text: Outsize, le roi omits nothing in fashioning of his period possibly

indicators.note: fashioning means shaping material anew, so the letters are rearranged
to omit nothing here literally means to leave out a zero-shaped letter from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
nothing is the round letter O, which is removed

explanation.surface: An oversized French king lacking nothing, dressed up in the fashion of his era.
explanation.walkthrough: OUTSIZE LE ROI minus one O is rearranged into LOUIS TREIZE, Louis XIII of France, whose name labels a period style of furniture and decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Treize names the French style of 1610 to 1643, so it could be the king's own period, giving the wordplay an &lit flavour.

clue.text: Second upward effort producing slice

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a heave is an effort to lift something

explanation.surface: A second attempt at lifting something results in a cut, perhaps of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives sheave as a dialect word for a slice, as of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheave is a dialect noun for a cut piece, so it is a rare synonym for a slice.

clue.text: Nothing mediocre in broadcast push for linked transmissions

indicators.note: in places the first two words inside what follows
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: OK means passable, merely middling
rearranged to HUPS
nothing is the round letter O

explanation.surface: Nothing so-so goes into a broadcasting campaign promoting a network link-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' sits naturally beside transmissions, but it only rearranges the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hook-ups are connections between broadcasting stations so that they carry one programme together.

clue.text: Malay vessels after prize ring Australia

parts.note: PR is a dictionary abbreviation for prize ring, a boxing ring
AUS is the international vehicle code for Australia

explanation.surface: Boats from Malaysia pursue a trophy around Australia, like a sailing race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' and 'ring' look separate, but the prize ring is old boxing, abbreviated PR.
explanation.definitionFit: A prau or proa is a fast Malay sailing boat, so the plural means several such craft.

clue.text: Short compositions, sort not played when nursing melancholy

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the rearranged letters cradle another word
played as in played around with, so the preceding words are worked into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, rearranged to RONTTOS
dole is an archaic word for grief or sorrow

explanation.surface: Brief musical pieces of a kind that are left unperformed while someone feels low.
explanation.walkthrough: Dole meaning sorrow is old-fashioned (compare doleful); it sits inside the shuffled SORT NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondoletto is a short rondo, a small-scale musical piece built on a returning theme.

clue.text: What one comes out with when fencing — it holds it up! (4, two words)

definitions.text: What one comes out with when fencing

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top
something that holds another has it inside

parts.note: the second 'it', SA again, turned upwards
'it' is sex appeal, abbreviated SA; this one is the outer part

explanation.surface: A fencer's battle cry, which the fencer then supposedly holds up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword staple; one SA holds the other upturned, S-AS-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Sa sa is an exclamation once used by fencers when thrusting, so it is what they call out mid-bout.

clue.text: It features experimental music — no Latin involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the two words are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A remark about avant-garde music that is free of any classical language.
explanation.walkthrough: Intonal is an experimental music festival held in Malmö, Sweden, so 'It' is the festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Intonal is a Swedish festival whose programme showcases experimental and electronic music.

clue.text: Enzyme complex that's modified generations

indicators.note: something modified has been altered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A biochemistry note about an enzyme that has changed over many lifetimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogenase is the enzyme complex in bacteria that fixes atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia.

clue.text: Sticky clay forming g-garland

parts.note: the stammered first letter supplies itself
a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland

explanation.surface: Gooey clay being shaped into a stuttered garland.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer 'g-' is a letter in its own right, placed before LEI.
explanation.definitionFit: Glei, or gley, is a sticky bluish-grey clay soil formed under waterlogged conditions.

clue.text: Love before work? Honor exercising reproductive gland

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: exercising puts something through its paces, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
the American spelling, rearranged to HORON

explanation.surface: A motto putting romance ahead of the job, with honour at work, in American spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just puts O ahead of OP; the American spelling of honor supplies the five letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oophoron is a medical name for the ovary, the female organ that produces eggs.

clue.text: Not quite scholarship grade in French and interrupting degree

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of something else

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree
'and' in French is et

explanation.surface: A marking below scholarship level in a French exam, with a degree being cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scholarship grade' points at alpha; second-class marks are graded beta.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second grade in the Greek-letter marking scale, one step short of the top alpha mark.

clue.text: US bumpkin having to get by (just) with little English

parts.note: to rub along is to manage, just about
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An American country yokel scraping by with hardly any English.
explanation.definitionFit: Rube is American slang for an unsophisticated rural person, a hick or yokel.

clue.text: Cordial advance? I arrange to be accepted

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so it goes inside the other word

parts.note: an ante is a stake paid in advance in poker
taken as written
to set is to arrange, as in setting a table

explanation.surface: A friendly overture, and someone hopes the plan they arranged will be welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' and 'advance' both look like friendliness, but cordial is the drink and the advance is a poker stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur, and a cordial is an old word for a liqueur.

clue.text: Religious decoration once created by Parvati and Lakshmi jointly

indicators.note: jointly means joined together, so the end of one name is attached to the start of the next

parts.note: the closing two letters of the first goddess's name
the opening three letters of the second goddess's name

explanation.surface: A sacred ornament said to have been made by two Hindu goddesses together.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a hidden word, but 'and' sits in the way: the tail of the first name is joined to the head of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilak is a mark worn on the forehead by Hindus as a sign of devotion or sect.

clue.text: Zoroastrians will have form of this Buddhist aim at heart

indicators.note: a form of something is a version reshaped, so the kept letters are rearranged
the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters of the first word are kept

parts.note: the central six of its twelve letters

explanation.surface: A claim that followers of Zoroaster secretly share a Buddhist spiritual goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle six letters of ZOROASTRIANS, OASTRI, rearrange to SATORI.
explanation.definitionFit: Satori is the Zen term for sudden enlightenment, the goal Zen practice seeks.

clue.text: Sower's basket: 'ave a care in cast

indicators.note: in places the cockney phrase inside the following word

parts.note: to slip is to cast off, as a snake its skin or an animal its young
'heed' with its H dropped, as the cockney 'ave signals

explanation.surface: A cockney warning to take care with a farmer's seed basket among the players.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in ''ave' tells you to drop the H of HEED too.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedlip is the basket a farmer carried when broadcasting seed by hand.

clue.text: Such singers e.g. are deployed in opera songs

indicators.note: deployed means spread out into position, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; these letters are part of the mix, so they come away from it
the anagram total

explanation.surface: An operatic remark that high female voices are used in arias.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus EG rearranges to OPERA SONGS, so remove E and G from OPERA SONGS and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sopranos are singers of the highest voice part, the kind the clue's singers are.

clue.text: Part of the family, as is told

explanation.surface: A family member, as the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for kin by blood or marriage and also the past participle of relate, to recount a story.

clue.text: Poet's lofty look, with little support within

indicators.note: within puts the support inside the word for look

parts.note: to spy is to look
a golf tee is a small peg supporting the ball

explanation.surface: A poet gazing upwards with a small prop holding things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' marks the answer as a poetic word, and the little support is the golf peg.
explanation.definitionFit: Steepy is a poetic form of steep, meaning high and sheer.

clue.text: For instance, getting on back is easy

indicators.note: back tells you to read the combined words from the end

parts.note: e.g. stands for exempli gratia, for example
someone getting on is growing old

explanation.surface: Supposedly getting on in years, looking back, is simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy' here means relaxed and unconstrained in manner, not simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Dégagé, from French, describes a relaxed, unconstrained manner, which is easy in the sense of casual.

clue.text: Shaggy monkey hiding in a glade

indicators.note: a hiding is a thrashing, and beaten letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A hairy primate lurking in a forest clearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding in' looks like a hidden-word signal, and the letters are all there, but not in order: a hiding is a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: The gelada is an Ethiopian baboon-like primate with a long shaggy mane.

clue.text: Body waste gets dispersed in running water

indicators.note: in places the scattered letters inside the word for running water

parts.note: ea is a dialect word for a river or running water

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: rearranged to GEST

explanation.surface: A sanitation report: excrement is carried away downstream.
explanation.walkthrough: EA, a river, is a dialect word Azed solvers meet often.
explanation.definitionFit: Egesta are materials discharged from the body, the opposite of ingesta taken in.

clue.text: Beer maker: soak's plot is holding recipe back

indicators.note: back tells you to read the whole assembled string from the end

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax; with the 's it becomes RETS

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside

parts.note: a web is a tangled scheme or plot
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on a prescription

explanation.surface: A brewer accused of plotting to keep a drunk's recipe secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' suggests a drunkard but is the flax-processing verb ret; the 's is part of the wordplay, and the whole string is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Brewster is an old word, originally for a woman, meaning a brewer of ale or beer.

clue.text: Sounds like springtime in Scotland for such clothes

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is pronounced as the word described

parts.note: ware is a Scots word for spring

explanation.surface: A note that a Scottish season gives its name to the outfits people put on then.
explanation.walkthrough: Ware is the Scots word for springtime; the answer is the word for clothing that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear as a noun means clothing, as in springwear or menswear, so such clothes are spring wear.

clue.text: Yearn misguidedly for old-style rule

indicators.note: something done misguidedly goes wrong, so the letters end up out of place

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Wrongly longing for the old ways of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayne is a Spenserian spelling of reign, a period of royal power or dominion.

clue.text: Well-known hymn setting, strangely muted round end of nave (6, two words)

indicators.note: round means going around, so the rearranged letters surround the last one
strangely means oddly, so the letters are put into an odd order

parts.note: rearranged to TEDUM

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of nave

explanation.surface: A famous hymn arrangement heard oddly hushed around the far end of a church nave.
explanation.definitionFit: The Te Deum is the ancient Latin hymn of praise, set to music by many composers.

clue.text: It's often dull, day after day

parts.note: Thu is the abbreviation for Thursday
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A complaint that life is tedious, one day after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'day' is placed first in the clue's reading: D comes after THU. 'Dull' means low and muffled in sound, not boring.
explanation.definitionFit: A thud is a heavy low sound, typically dull and muffled rather than sharp.

clue.text: Press to clarify dropping opening page

indicators.note: dropping the opening means losing the first letter

parts.note: to purge is to clear or make clean
P is the abbreviation for page, and it is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: Pushing for something to be cleared up by removing its first page.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to urge them, both meaning to push or insist strongly.

clue.text: Dior-esque typically? Braggart may shoot it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the flared dress shape Christian Dior introduced
second meaning: a boaster shoots ..., read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: To shoot a line is British slang for boasting or exaggerating.
explanation.definitionFit: Dior launched the A-line silhouette in 1955, narrow above and flaring below; split, the letters also make the article plus boastful line.

clue.text: Merriment? Term restricts it

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the term encloses the other word

parts.note: Hilary is the spring term at Oxford and in the law courts
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a school term limited by fun, or the fun limited by the term?
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary is the name of the term running from January at Oxford, Dublin and the English law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is loud laughter and high spirits, a synonym for merriment.

clue.text: Making one like gossip aplenty?

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
as can mean like, in the manner of

explanation.surface: A question about what would turn a person into a lover of tittle-tattle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the plural of ana, a collection of someone's sayings and gossip; several of them is plenty of gossip, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers defines ana as a collection of anecdotes or table-talk, so many of these mean plenty of gossip.

clue.text: Fertilizer scattered on bed, unserviceable with time

indicators.note: scattered means strewn about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: rearranged to BONED
u/s is short for unserviceable
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A gardener spreads plant food over a flower bed that has worn out over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scattered' fits the fertilizer picture but only shuffles ON BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonedust is ground animal bone spread on soil as a phosphate-rich manure.

clue.text: Papers in fact are acting for slum district (13, two words)

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the word for fact

parts.note: in fact means in deed, actually
the press is newspapers collectively
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in a job title

explanation.surface: Newspapers report actors playing a run-down neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fact' splits away from 'in': fact alone is the deed, and A for acting is a job-title abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A depressed area is a region suffering economic decline and poverty, a run-down part of a town.
